body:
## Description

This PR adds the dependencies for resolving https://github.com/canonical/checkbox/issues/1868 and https://github.com/canonical/checkbox/pull/1677

This may looks like a lot of dependencies but the bulk of the library is already in checkbox with the base glmark2 package. All the other glmark2 variants share the same "assets" like 3d model files with base glmark2. The extra stuff we are installing are the main executable files which are pretty small

```bash
# after installing just glmark2
❯ sudo apt install glmark2-es2 glmark2-es2-wayland glmark2-wayland
Reading package lists... Done

  glmark2-es2-wayland glmark2-es2-x11 glmark2-wayland
0 upgraded, 3 newly installed, 0 to remove and 1 not upgraded.
Need to get 693 kB of archives.
After this operation, 1,916 kB of additional disk space will be used.
```

## Resolved issues

<!--

Make sure that the linked issue titles & descriptions are also up to date.
-->

## Documentation

The only thing I'm not sure about are the dependencies for ubuntu 16 and 18. I've checked that the packages exist on them and can be `apt install`'ed, but I'm not sure why it wasn't there before in their snapcraft.yaml files.

## Tests

Manually checked that the packages exist on 16 ~ 24

author: thaddeuskkr
body:
this PR improves the current docker build workflow, does the following:

- pushes image for testing on pull requests (tags with `pr-[id]` and commit sha (short), e.g., `pr-32`, etc.)
- builds multiarch images using docker bake (currently set to `linux/amd64` and `linux/arm64`, can be customised in `docker-bake.hcl`)
- builds arm64 images using specific github hosted runners, builds all platforms simultaneously using matrixes
- tags images with commit sha and branch rather than just `latest`, allows users to rollback changes themselves

this pull request will fix issue #244

author: versusfacit
body:
## Problem
So we need to accommodate fields higher than 128 bytes in some cases. The Go Library is proven to support arbitrary lengths but this Rust layer artificially constrains values. This is a problem because some tokens go well beyond 128-1 bytes (-1 for the null terminator).

This bug was encountered while trying to use `Database::set_option` and `Database::get_option` for a string higher than 128 bytes in length. `Database::set_option` doesn't have this restriction curiously.

## Impact

Without this functionality, we cannot complete native oauth in Snowflake.

Other database configurations with values longer than 128 bytes will not be supported.


## Solution
To always allocate 1024 truly would be overkill. So I'm splitting the difference with 1024 bytes.

I'm stabbing a bit in the dark here but I think the type to override for will be `c_char`.

If you know a more efficient workaround, please, let's do that, not this :D

body:
### Ticket
N/A

### Problem description
Building the tt-mlir repo takes a long time (sometimes over 30 min on CI), especially for a fresh build

### What's changed
When clang is used as the compiler, try to find and use the matching lld linker
The same linker is passed to the tt-metal external project as well
Detect the `CPM_SOURCE_CACHE` environment variable and pass it to the tt-metal build command, so we don't re-download the 1.4 GB tt-metal external dependencies every time, if the environment variable is set to some out-of-tree location
Set up persistent cmake CPM cache in the CI

### Checklist
- [x] New/Existing tests provide coverage for changes

author: urmauur
body:
## Describe Your Changes

This pull request introduces enhancements to the `MCPConfiguration` component in the `web/screens/Settings/MCP/configuration.tsx` file. The changes focus on improving the user experience when editing configuration files, particularly by sanitizing input and maintaining cursor position during updates.

### Enhancements to input handling and user experience:

* **Added `useRef` for TextArea reference**: Introduced a `textAreaRef` using `useRef` to manage the cursor position during updates. (`[[1]](diffhunk://#diff-32acd7247a078095f811607a2902c02bc7070611281ad58c813cb49e1813c322L1-R1)`, `[[2]](diffhunk://#diff-32acd7247a078095f811607a2902c02bc7070611281ad58c813cb49e1813c322R15-R16)`)
* **Sanitized quotes in input**: Implemented logic to replace curly quotes (`“”` and `‘’`) with straight quotes (`"` and `'`) to ensure consistent formatting of the configuration content. (`[web/screens/Settings/MCP/configuration.tsxL79-R111](diffhunk://#diff-32acd7247a078095f811607a2902c02bc7070611281ad58c813cb49e1813c322L79-R111)`)
* **Restored cursor position**: Used `requestAnimationFrame` to restore the cursor position after DOM updates caused by sanitization. This ensures a seamless editing experience for the user. (`[web/screens/Settings/MCP/configuration.tsxL79-R111](diffhunk://#diff-32acd7247a078095f811607a2902c02bc7070611281ad58c813cb49e1813c322L79-R111)`)

### Accessibility and usability improvements:

* **Disabled browser auto-features**: Added `autoComplete="off"`, `autoCorrect="off"`, and `spellCheck={false}` to the `TextArea` to prevent unwanted browser interventions while editing JSON configuration files. (`[web/screens/Settings/MCP/configuration.tsxL79-R111](diffhunk://#diff-32acd7247a078095f811607a2902c02bc7070611281ad58c813cb49e1813c322L79-R111)`)


## Fixes Issues

![Screenshot 2025-04-21 at 09 42 06](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/dbccf74f-5422-421f-8c4e-d33330d273df)

- Closes # https://discord.com/channels/1107178041848909847/1362449620239909167
- Closes #

- [ ] Added relevant comments, esp in complex areas
- [ ] Updated docs (for bug fixes / features)
- [ ] Created issues for follow-up changes or refactoring needed

author: krokicki
body:
This PR adds support for absolute URIs that are specified in the metadata file, e.g. 
```
python -m zarrcade.import -c open-organelle -i open-organelle-zarr.txt
```

Where `open-organelle-zarr.txt` looks like this: 
```
uri     name    type    grid    description     thumbnail_url   image_format    organism        cell_type       cell_subtype    treatment
s3://janelia-cosem-datasets/cam_hum-airway-14500/cam_hum-airway-14500.zarr/recon-1/em/fibsem-uint8/     cam_hum-airway-14500    intensities     em      " Human Airway Epithelium, from human primary nasal basal stem cell progenitors, differentiated using Air Liquid Interphase (ALI) cultures"   https://janelia-cosem-datasets.s3.amazonaws.com/cam_hum-airway-14500/thumbnail.jpg    zarr                            
```

This will skip the Zarr discovery step and directly create images in the database based on the URIs given in the input file. It also looks for a column containing the word "thumbnail" to use for importing existing thumbnail images.

With this PR, Zarrcade can be input-compatible with either [Bio FileFinder](https://github.com/AllenInstitute/biofile-finder) or [MoBIE](https://github.com/mobie/mobie-viewer-fiji) (though the compatibility isn't bidirectional and there is currently no way to make an input spreadsheet that is compatible with all three).

author: taoyang526
body:
### Ⅰ. Describe what this PR does

The ElasticQuota plugin is designed to manage quotas dynamically. To enhance its flexibility and extensibility, this proposal introduces the `QuotaHookPlugin` interface. This interface allows custom logic to be injected into various stages of quota management, such as pre-update, post-update, and pod updates. 

Based on this interface, custom resource limits can be extended to meet the needs of more fine-grained resource management. For example, it enables limiting resource usage for specific workloads such as Spark Drivers or other specialized tasks, providing enhanced control and optimization for diverse application scenarios.

#### Changes Overview
1. **QuotaHookPlugin Interface**: Defined a new interface `QuotaHookPlugin` with methods like `IsQuotaUpdated`, `PreQuotaUpdate`, `PostQuotaUpdate`, `UpdateQuotaStatus`, `OnPodUpdated`, and `CheckPod`. These methods enable plugins to participate in different phases of quota lifecycle management.

2. **Factory Pattern**: Implemented a factory pattern for registering and initializing hook plugins. This ensures plugins can be dynamically loaded based on configuration.

3. **Initialization Logic**: Enhanced the initialization logic in `InitHookPlugins` to load and configure plugins from the provided `ElasticQuotaArgs`.

4. **GroupQuotaManager Enhancements**: Extended the `GroupQuotaManager` to support running pre-update, post-update, and pod update hooks. Methods like `runPreQuotaUpdateHooks`, `runPostQuotaUpdateHooks`, and `runPodUpdateHooks` were added to execute these hooks.

5. **Metrics Integration**: Added a `MetricsWrapper` to wrap `QuotaHookPlugin` instances, recording latency metrics for each operation. Metrics are exposed via Prometheus-compatible histograms.

- Khi cancel đơn  thì lịch sử booking ở bàn tương ứng cũng sẽ bị xóa

This pull request introduces several updates to the CloudStack provider, including enhancements to network configuration, dependency upgrades, and validation logic improvements. The changes also include a migration to the Uber `mock` library for mocking in tests. Below are the most important changes grouped by theme: ### Network Configuration Enhancements: * Added a `NetworkMode` field to the `Network` and `CloudStackIsolatedNetworkStatus` structs to support routing mode configurations. This field is also reflected in the CRDs (`cloudstackclusters.yaml`, `cloudstackfailuredomains.yaml`, `cloudstackisolatednetworks.yaml`). [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-b2d8e021994f6dd6ed5dc9b5d73c5f1120833d9c2ad8ad0e37f7109b58bb4701R75-R78) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-a21ce8b2338c3cdd47ae1360ef78c3d50ab5c3a58e258ed13b610f76ef96aecdR71-R73) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-802196d20b6ef0499bf5b72ba67d6b5d2d6f8e1b6e21f25e9dcad6f215b143f6R428-R430) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-30eda3e0df3d10eed0cf5340750691bbe8b1fa7ae2b628f4dcb41c0966ce0949R196-R198) [[5]](diffhunk://#diff-155096c9f99ba521cd09a2a4f931d6d58915eb733da5c7c4930cf674e2f28257R257-R259) * Updated the `Network()` method of `CloudStackIsolatedNetwork` to include the `NetworkMode` from its status. * Added logic to handle `NetworkMode` in the `AddToLBIfNeeded` method, ensuring that load balancer assignment is skipped for routed networks. ### Validation Logic Improvements: * Modified the `ValidateUpdate` method in `CloudStackCluster` to allow updates to the `ControlPlaneEndpoint.Host` field while ensuring the `Port` remains unchanged. ### Dependency and Tooling Updates: * Migrated from `github.com/golang/mock` to `go.uber.org/mock` for mocking in tests, updating all relevant test files and the `Makefile`. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-74a6a4b491f8c4cc6ff00dd4562f8b97772c0ecfd368284ff8a720320017b528L20-R22) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-1ec63830f0b8ad2346b09376fe262fb481f08bb809008a644acb8b76470d1d92L20-R22) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-20ac05b50e2231b1dfe413d6c82ce50018f9200458d8067994f52bc50a965818L20-R22) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-2813be8e0c499cf807a285ab84a7e382d854ea93f8d9a5027618f12a460b2a3fL20-R22) [[5]](diffhunk://#diff-310f3c4f634c685d9715210471368da3482a13e6fef14f51644148f35a7e8463L20-R22) [[6]](diffhunk://#diff-0df3f4ad855bcb84e029d6081548d4d90036291793e9014a036eebb60bc85d0bL20-R22) [[7]](diffhunk://#diff-6667c8c8563cbf8319af48cd19055f1c4fe7590294de12524bed9ba2fa1e788cL23-R25) [[8]](diffhunk://#diff-16fcc5e8a0a88d0911611868ee7144794cae7738630a91e4178f6ca64f358d6dL40-R43) [[9]](diffhunk://#diff-c47c440e8e5516ae4488dfc528596e467a16db07cd501de44ee6c5b7c0de1a03L23-R25) [[10]](diffhunk://#diff-e10dbadfede00dfda2bb17122cea24cb3e922bd6c051d6e801c29856bb6027d8L140-R140) * Upgraded Go version to 1.23 and updated dependencies in `go.mod` files, including `cloudstack-go` to v2.17.0 and `golangci-lint` to v1.60.2. author: mayansharma
body:
This PR includes
1. A template app built on our getting started guide
2. Test cases for the template app
3. A pipeline yml file to run build and test cases commands

---



---



 **DeputyDev generated PR summary:** 



---



 **Size XXL:** This PR changes include 1000+ lines and should take approximately 6+ hours to review, potentially spread across multiple sessions



---

The pull request titled "Test cases - template app + pipeline" introduces several changes and additions to the repository. Here's a summary of what the PR does:

1. **CI Pipeline Update**:
   - The GitHub Actions workflow for Node.js has been updated. The previous jobs for linting, building, and testing have been consolidated into a single `build` job using a matrix strategy for Node.js version 20.4.0.
   - The workflow is now triggered on pull requests targeting the `main` branch instead of the `master` branch.
   - The job uses `npm ci` for installing dependencies, which is generally faster and more reliable for CI environments than `npm install`.

2. **Template Application Setup**:
   - A new template application structure has been added, including client and server-side code.
   - The application appears to be a demo for a Dog Adoption Center, utilizing React and server-side rendering capabilities.
   - The template includes configurations for routing, styling, and API interactions, with a focus on server-side rendering using Catalyst.

3. **Playwright Configuration**:
   - A Playwright configuration file has been added for end-to-end testing, supporting different environments (dev and prod) and multiple browsers (Chromium, Firefox, WebKit).

4. **New Files and Directories**:
   - Various new files and directories have been introduced, including components, pages, styles, and configuration files.
   - The `.eslintignore` and `.eslintrc` files are added to configure ESLint rules and ignore patterns for the template directory.

5. **Scripts and Dependencies**:
   - The `package.json` files have been updated to include new scripts for building, serving, and testing the application.
   - New dependencies and devDependencies have been added to support the application's functionality, including Playwright for testing and ESLint for code linting.

6. **Static Assets and Styles**:
   - SCSS files for styling have been added, along with a favicon for the application.

7. **Testing**:
   - New test cases have been added using Playwright to ensure the application renders correctly, fetches data as expected, and handles server middleware responses.

Overall, this PR sets up a comprehensive template application with a CI pipeline, testing, and server-side rendering capabilities.

---

This includes the removal of managed identity credential setup and external identity registration. ### Dependency Upgrades:
* Upgraded the `Aspire.Hosting.AppHost` package from version `9.0.0` to `9.2.0` in `AspireDemo1.AppHost`.

author: thomasheartman
body:
Removes the condition to hide the value list if we use legal values. 

In doing so, I also realized that focus handling when you delete the last item in the constraint values list doesn't work if the add values button isn't there (which it shouldn't be for legal values and more). So I've hidden the add values button when it doesn't do anythnig helpful (or for cases where we don't have designs yet). In cases where you don't have the add values button and you delete the last constraint value, we'll move the focus to the "delete constraint" button (that was easier than making sure we pass refs all the way down into the operator select, but we can change that later).

To facilitate this (refs coming from the parent component), I refactored the value list component to accept the add values widget as a child (and extracted it to its own file).

## Functionality
- Move IAST langchain integration to use event hub callbacks.
- Support IAST propagation through LLM invocations. If any LLM prompt is tainted, then any LLM output is fully tainted too.

author: mergify[bot]
body:
This is an automatic copy of pull request #11577 done by [Mergify](https://mergify.com).

----

## Issue

https://gravitee.atlassian.net/browse/APIM-9418

## Description

While testing the Homescreen dashboard, I noticed a bug that only affects users without the Admin role.

If you're using the Gravitee Console with an Admin role, everything works as expected—you can view all APIs and their metrics.

However, if you're logged in with **any role other than ADMIN** (e.g., **USER**), you'll likely encounter an error similar to the one shown below:
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c8386dfb-fef1-4e8e-8bf7-04edac40b2dc)


## Additional context

**Bug Explanation**
When a user with a non-admin role (e.g., USER) accesses certain environmental analytics, they trigger permission checks like the following:

```
@Permissions({
  @Permission(value = RolePermission.API_ANALYTICS, acls = { RolePermissionAction.READ })
})
```

Since this check references API_ANALYTICS, it assumes that the call is tied to a specific API. The system tries to validate access by extracting the API ID from the request URI, using UriInfo in the requestContext.

**The issue:**
When the call is coming from the dashboard, the URI doesn't contain an API ID—so the lookup fails. Specifically, getId() in PermissionFilter.java (line 114) returns null, and access is denied.

Admins bypass this issue because the permission check is short-circuited early for users with admin rights.

**Fix:**
Removed permission checks for the buggy dashboard analytics. The initial v4 analytics didn’t include these checks, so this change restores consistency with existing behavior.

Only 4 widgets were affected.
The remaining widgets function correctly as they don’t implement these permission checks.

## Type of changes

## Checklist

## Description
This PR adds support for indeterminate progress bars that show elapsed time and expected total, addressing issue #3572. Linked here https://github.com/Textualize/rich/issues/3572

### Problem
Users requested a way to display progress bars in an indeterminate state (animated pulse) while still showing elapsed time and an indicator like `?/total`. Currently, using `start=False` or `total=None` either doesn't show elapsed time or doesn't allow for the desired display format.

### Solution
- Added `indeterminate` and `expected_total` parameters to tasks
- Created new rendering logic for indeterminate progress bars with animated pulsing effect
- Added `IndeterminateTaskProgressColumn` to display `?/total` for indeterminate tasks
- Preserved elapsed time display during indeterminate state
- Enabled smooth transition from indeterminate to determinate state

### Features Added
- Indeterminate progress bars show animated pulse with elapsed time
- Tasks can be created with `indeterminate=True` and optional `expected_total`
- New `IndeterminateTaskProgressColumn` displays `?/total` for indeterminate tasks
- Seamless transition from indeterminate to determinate (green 100%) completion
- Comprehensive test coverage for new functionality

### Example Usage
```python
with Progress() as progress:
    # Create an indeterminate task with expected total
    task_id = progress.add_task(
        "Indexing",
        indeterminate=True,
        expected_total=10
    )
    
    # Later, convert to determinate
    progress.update(
        task_id,
        indeterminate=False,
        total=10,
        completed=10
    )

This pull request enhances the `calculetes` library by introducing a new feature for numerical differentiation, updating the documentation, and adding comprehensive tests for the new functionality. The most important changes include the addition of a `Derivative` class, updates to the README to reflect the new feature, and test coverage for the derivative calculations.

### New Feature: Numerical Differentiation

* Added a `Derivative` class that supports numerical differentiation using forward, backward, and central difference methods. It allows users to calculate derivatives of any order with configurable step size. (`packages/calculetes/src/derivative/index.ts`)
* Exported the `Derivative` class in the library's main entry point for public use. (`packages/calculetes/src/index.ts`)

### Documentation Updates

* Updated the README to include details about the `Derivative` class, its usage, and configuration options. The documentation now provides examples for both integrals and derivatives. (`packages/calculetes/readme.md`)

### Test Coverage

* Added comprehensive test cases for the `Derivative` class, covering first-order and higher-order derivatives, different approximation methods, step size effects, and error handling. (`packages/calculetes/tests/derivate.test.ts`)

body:
<!-- Anything that looks like this is a comment and can't be seen after the Pull Request is created. -->

# PR Summary
Change remoting config file (`%windir%\System32\PowerShell\7.5.0\RemotePowerShellConfig.txt`) reader to use an input stream instead of an input/output stream. This means that write access is no longer needed in this system directory.
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2288e81f-f85e-4eb8-9c03-db2bebd3096a)


<!-- Summarize your PR between here and the checklist. -->

## PR Context
This should help with issues:
https://github.com/MicrosoftDocs/PowerShell-Docs/issues/11682
https://github.com/PowerShell/PowerShell/issues/18741
https://github.com/PowerShell/PowerShell/issues/20180
https://github.com/PowerShell/PowerShell/issues/14274
https://github.com/PowerShell/PowerShell/issues/17367

## Tip
For completeness sake, I will mention that if you change `(Get-PSSessionConfiguration -Name <session_config_name>).Filename` to point at the dll that is present in PowerShell's install location (e.g. `"C:\Program Files\PowerShell\7\pwrshplugin.dll"`) it should work without write permissions, with the added benefit of always having this file auto-updated when a new version of PowerShell is installed.

Excellent write up in https://awakecoding.com/posts/enable-powershell-winrm-remoting-in-powershell-7/ shows the command to do that:
```
Set-Item -Path "WSMan:\localhost\Plugin\PowerShell.7\Filename" -Value $WSManPluginPath
```

author: richterrettich
body:
DNF repositories represent the binary RPM metadata in XML. Some metadata that is stored is related to sizes, e.G: `<rpm:header-range start="4504" end="17328"/>`
The given example metadata effectively says "Header starts at 4504 and ends at 17328"
This patch implements the necessary methods to calculate these sizes:
```rust
let end = pkg.metadata.get_total_metadata_size();
let start = end - pkg.metadata.header.size();
```

author: paulinebanye
body:
### **Description**
This PR addresses the `unpickleable configuration value` warning encountered during the Sphinx `make html` build process (Issue #1202).

The warning arises because the matplotlib_skore_scraper function in sphinx_gallery_conf (defined in conf.py) cannot be serialized by Python’s pickle module.

```python
# configuration cache warning
- pickling environment... WARNING: cannot cache unpickable configuration value: 'sphinx_gallery_conf' (because it contains a function, class, or module object) [config.cache]
```

---

### **Environment**

- Model: Dell Latitude E7440
- RAM: 12GB 
- OS: Windows 10 pro
- Python Version: Python 3.12
- Terminal: Ubuntu 22.04 LTS

---


### **Steps to reproduce:**
1. Clone the skore repository
2. Create and activate a virtual environment using the Ubuntu terminal
3. Run the _make install-skore_ command.
4. Cd into the sphinx directory
5. Run `make html`.
---

### **Proposed Solutions**
There are several ways this warning can be resolved.
1: Using the built-in Matplotlib scraper
- Pros: It is simple to maintain and has no pickling issues.
- Cons: Requires extra configuration to make it match the custom function defined in sphinxext/matplotlib_skore_scraper.py.

```python
# in conf.py
import matplotlib
matplotlib.rcParams['savefig.bbox'] = 'tight' # extra configuration to match the custom scraper function

sphinx_gallery_conf = {
    "image_scrapers": ['matplotlib'], # use the built-in matplotlib scraper
}
```

2. Converting the custom matplotlib_skore_scraper function to a class. 
- Pros: This option is flexible,  serializable and can be customized further, if required.
- Cons: More complex than using the built-in scraper.

```python
# in matplotlib_skore_scraper.py
class matplotlib_skore_scraper:
    def __call__(self, *args, **kwargs):
        kwargs.setdefault("bbox_inches", "tight")
        return matplotlib_scraper(*args, **kwargs)

# in conf.py
sphinx_gallery_conf = {
    "image_scrapers": [matplotlib_skore_scraper()],
}
```

3. Defining the Scraper Directly in conf.py: This requires adding the custom matplotlib_skore_scraper function directly in the conf.py file. 
- Pros: No pickling issue or import errors when importing the function from a different file.
- Cons: It would clutter the conf.py file.

```python
# in conf.py
def __call__(self, *args, **kwargs):
   kwargs.setdefault("bbox_inches", "tight")
   return matplotlib_scraper(*args, **kwargs)

sphinx_gallery_conf = {
    "image_scrapers": [matplotlib_skore_scraper],
}
```

4. Supressing the warning. 
Pros: No major code change required. 
Cons: It does not address the root cause of this warning, and it would mask other caching issues because it is declared globally.
```python
# in conf.py
suppress_warnings = [
   'config.cache'  # silence config warnings
]
```

---

I chose the class option, because it resolves the pickling issue, it is flexible and keeps the code organized. However, I'm happy to modify this if another solution would work better.

cc @sylvaincom @glemaitre @thomass-dev

## Pull Request: Add Bitcoin Market Data Analysis Notebook and README

### Summary

This pull request adds a complete Jupyter notebook and a concise README for analyzing Bitcoin (BTC-USD) market data. The project implements a full data pipeline that includes data fetching, storage, analysis, and visualization using the CoinMarketCap API and SQLite.

### Changes Introduced

- Added `sqlite.analysis.ipynb`:
  - Retrieves 15 years of historical BTC-USD data
  - Fetches real-time market data from CoinMarketCap
  - Stores and updates data in a local SQLite database (`btcDaily.db`)
  - Performs SQL and Python-based statistical analyses
  - Includes visualizations such as moving averages, Bollinger Bands, rate of change, and volatility trends

- Added `README.md`:
  - Outlines project objectives, structure, setup steps, and workflow
  - Provides usage instructions and documentation references
  - Summarizes key analyses and visual outputs

### Motivation

This addition enables reproducible and extensible cryptocurrency market analysis using open-source tools. It serves as a base for exploring historical trends, detecting volatility patterns, and understanding BTC market dynamics.

### Notes

- CoinMarketCap API key is required for live data functionality.
- All dependencies are listed in the README setup section.
- The notebook follows modular and clean coding practices to ensure maintainability.

None at this time.

-------------------------

- Setuptools no longer accepts options containing uppercase or dash characters in ``setup.cfg``.
  Please ensure to write the options in ``setup.cfg`` using the :wiki:`lower_snake_case <Snake_case>` convention
  (e.g. ``Name => name``, ``install-requires => install_requires``).
  This is a follow-up on deprecations introduced in
  `v54.1.0 <https://setuptools.pypa.io/en/latest/history.html#v54-1-0>`_ (see 1608) and
  `v54.1.1 <https://setuptools.pypa.io/en/latest/history.html#v54-1-1>`_ (see 2592).

  .. note::
     This change *does not affect configurations in* ``pyproject.toml``
     (which uses the :wiki:`lower-kebab-case <Letter_caseKebab_case>` convention following the precedent set in :pep:`517`/:pep:`518`). (4870)

   ### 77.0.0

   =======

Features
--------

- Added initial support for license expression (PEP :pep:`639 <639add-license-expression-field>`). -- by :user:`cdce8p` (4706)
- Store ``License-File``\s in ``.dist-info/licenses`` subfolder and added support for recursive globs for ``license_files`` (PEP :pep:`639 <639add-license-expression-field>`). -- by :user:`cdce8p` (4728)
- Bump core metadata version to ``2.4``\. -- by :user:`cdce8p` (4830)

Deprecations and Removals
-------------------------

- Added initial implementation of :pep:`639`.
  Users relying on pre- :pep:`639` implementation details
  (like precise license file paths inside ``dist-info`` directory)
  may need to adjust their code base to avoid problems.
  Deprecations and stronger validation were also introduced (4829).
- Added exception (or warning) when deprecated license classifiers are used,

  ``project.license-files`` and/or SPDX expressions (as strings) in
  ``project.license``\.
  See PEP :pep:`639 <639deprecate-license-key-table-subkeys>`. (4840)
- Added simple validation for given glob patterns in ``license-files``\:
  a warning will be generated if no file is matched.
  Invalid glob patterns can raise an exception.

## References

[MAJC-61](https://mozilla-hub.atlassian.net/browse/MAJC-61)

## Problem Statement

We have great unit test coverage in this repo, but we don't yet have any automated cross-browser testing or end-to-end testing. Additionally, we don't have any testing that verifies how the current dist bundle behaves on our React and IIFE example surfaces. 

## Proposed Changes

Add the Playwright testing library and create some tests, as well as a CI job. 

Currently implemented tests are:

* Display the ad/ ad layout for all formats on IIFE and React, on mobile and desktop browsers
* Click and navigation to the landing page on all formats, IIFE and React, on mobile and desktop browsers

Still to add tests are:
* Context Id
* Reporting flow
* Tricky tests for impression and click callbacks
* Tests for fallback ad
* Something weird going on with the Skyscraper and mobile chrome

## Verification Steps

- [ ] Pull the branch, install the dependency, and make sure it runs locally
- [ ] Check how it looks in CI

author: mrmelbert
body:
## About The Pull Request

Melee attack chain now has a list passed along with it, `attack_modifiers`, which you can stick force modifiers to change the resulting attack

This is basically a soft implementation of damage packets until a more definitive pr, but one that only applies to item attack chain, and not unarmed attacks.

This change was done to facilitate a baton refactor - batons no longer hack together their own attack chain, and are now integrated straight into the real attack chain. This refactor itself was done because batons don't send any attack signals, which has been annoying in the past (for swing combat).

## Changelog

:cl: Melbert
refactor: Batons have been refactored again. Baton stuns now properly count as an attack, when before it was a nothing. Report any oddities, particularly in regards to harmbatonning vs normal batonning.
refactor: The method of adjusting item damage mid-attack has been refactored - some affected items include the Nullblade and knives. Report any strange happenings with damage numbers.
refactor: A few objects have been moved to the new interaction chain - records consoles, mawed crucible, alien weeds and space vines, hedges, restaurant portals,  and some mobs - to name a few. 
fix: Spears only deal bonus damage against secure lockers, not all closet types (including crates) 
/:cl:

author: anonfedora
body:
# 📦 PR Title:  
**feat: Implement Contributor Reputation and Credential Verification Smart Contract**

# 📝 Description:
Closes #68
This PR introduces the **Contributor Reputation and Credential Verification Contract** for the Akkuea platform. It implements all the functionality outlined in [[Contract Issue #68](https://github.com/akkuea/issues/68)](https://github.com/akkuea/issues/68), including contributor reputation tracking, credential verification, and expertise area management.

Key components added:
- **Smart Contract Structure**:
  - `lib.rs`: Main contract configuration and exports.
  - `credentials.rs`: Non-transferable credential token minting and management.
  - `reputation.rs`: Subject-specific reputation tracking.
  - `expertise.rs`: Managing user expertise areas and levels.
  - `verify.rs`: User credential and content verification logic.
  - `error.rs`: Centralized error handling.
  - `types.rs`: Core data structures (`User`, `CredentialToken`, `Reputation`).
  - `test.rs`: Comprehensive test suite covering all major functionalities.

- **Development Setup**:
  - Added `Cargo.toml` with `soroban-sdk` dependencies.
  - Added `Makefile` for common operations (`build`, `test`, `fmt`, `clean`).
  - Added `.gitignore` for Rust/Soroban project artifacts.
  - Added README.md aligning with Soroban project structure.

# ✅ Features Implemented:
- User Registration (`initialize_user`, `get_user`).
- Expertise Areas Management (`update_expertise_areas`, `get_expertise_areas`).
- Non-Transferable Credential Token Minting (`mint_credential_token`).
- Subject-Specific Reputation Management (`update_reputation`, `get_reputation`).
- User Verification Process (`verify_user`).
- Content Verification Restricted to Verified and Expert Users (`verify_content`).

# 🧪 Testing:
![Screenshot_20250426_181235](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/243a9bd5-7904-4053-9480-19820a20bc1e)

- **Full unit test coverage** implemented in `src/test.rs`.
- Tests include:
  - User initialization and retrieval.
  - Minting credential tokens (positive and negative cases).
  - Updating and retrieving expertise areas.
  - Updating and retrieving reputation scores.
  - Verification logic validations for users and content.
  - Error cases for invalid operations like double-verification, unauthorized updates, and invalid expertise.

# 📈 Impact:
- Enhances trust within the Akkuea ecosystem by securely linking contributor credentials and reputation.
- Enforces verification constraints to ensure only credible contributors can validate and verify content.
- Establishes a scalable foundation for expanding contributor and expertise management.

# ⏳ ETA:
Completed within the 3-day target as planned.

# 📌 Additional Notes:
- This version is modular and ready for further integration with Akkuea's broader user/resource management system.
- Smart contract security and best practices have been prioritized.

Latejoining onto ships now starts you off as a hologram.  Both the hologram and the captain of the ship need to approve the process in order to actually join the ship.  Anyone with a deed to the ship is considered an acting captain, and you _must currently have the ID on you_.

If the captain or applicant wish to leave, they can at any time.  The captain interacts with the hologram through right click (ideally left click brings up a rotary menu).

Holograms cannot interact with the world, though they aren't ghosts - they take the (approximate) physical appearance of their character.  Ghosting from a hologram should delete it and reopen the job slot, the hologram should not be able to leave the ship or meaningfully interact with the world.

The feature is currently missing the ability to prevent a user by ID from rejoining the crew.

## Why / Balance
<!-- Discuss how this would affect game balance or explain why it was changed. Link any relevant discussions or issues. -->

Latejoin QOL and usability.

## Technical details
<!-- Summary of code changes for easier review. -->

New system, new component for tracking interview hologram entities, and new entities for hologram types.  There are new jobs (Contractor/Pilot/Merc Applicant) that start out as these holograms, and all shuttles are swapped over to use these new job slots.

## How to test
<!-- Describe a procedure to test this feature, along with expected output/behavior. -->

1. Start two clients.  On client 2, ensure your character has merc/pilot/contractor loadouts with a known cost.
2. Buy a ship on client 1, move over to the ship, open two contractor slots.  Make sure your ID is in your PDA, which is in your ID slot.
3. Latejoin the ship on client 2, you should start as a hologram with two actions.
4. On client 1, the captain's PDA should ring and you should get a notification (you should hear it on both clients).
5. Press the paper on fire action, you should return to the lobby and have a notification that you left in the chat.
7. Eject the ID from client 1's PDA.
8. On client 2, rejoin the ship (there should still be two slots open).
9. Press the Approve button.
10. On client 1, right click the hologram, "Approve" should be disabled.
11. Pick up the captain's ID.
12. Right click the hologram again and press "Approve".
13. The character should be replaced with their actual character.
14. Check the station records, your character details should show up and be correct.
15. Check the criminal records, your character details should show up and be correct.
16. Respawn on client 2.  Your loadout cost should be deducted from your funds.
17. Rejoin as an applicant (there should be one contractor slot left open).
18. On client 1, right click on the hologram, press "dismiss".  Client 2 should exit back to the lobby, have a message telling them they were dismissed, and the slot should remain open.
19. On client 2, rejoin as a Contractor Applicant, should still be open with one slot.
20. On client 1, right click on the hologram, select "Dismiss and Close".  Client 2 should exit back to the lobby, have a message telling them they were dismissed, and the slot should be closed.

## Media

Small fixes/refactors are exempt. Media may be used in SS14 progress reports with credit. -->

A slime hologram applies for a contractor job on a Pioneer.  Note the actions in the top left of the screen.  The captain of the ship is present for the interview.

body:
## Description
This PR modifies our kennel API to fetch data from a SQLite database instead of in-memory data structures. The changes include:

1. Updated all GET request handlers in `views` directory to query the SQLite database
2. Removed `top_selling_pet` parameter from `Location` class constructor
3. Added `Customer` import to `models/__init__.py`
4. Added SQL queries to `kennel.sql` for retrieving specific records
5. Fixed a redundant response writing in `request_handler.py`

## Related Issue
- N/A

## Motivation and Context
This change is necessary to persist data across server restarts and to enable more robust data querying capabilities. The in-memory data structures were insufficient for production use as all data would be lost when the server was restarted.

## How Can This Be Tested?
1. Run the server using `python kennel.py`
2. Use Postman or similar tool to make GET requests to the following endpoints:
   - GET `/animals` - Should return all animals from the database
   - GET `/animals/3` - Should return a single animal with id 3
   - GET `/locations` - Should return all locations from the database  
   - GET `/locations/1` - Should return a single location with id 1
   - GET `/employees` - Should return all employees from the database
   - GET `/employees/4` - Should return a single employee with id 4
   - GET `/customers` - Should return all customers from the database
   - GET `/customers/2` - Should return a single customer with id 2

## Screenshots (if appropriate):
N/A

## Types of changes
- [ ] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [x] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- [x] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to change)

## Type
- [x] Component
- [ ] Page
- [ ] Bugfix
- [ ] Style
- [ ] Refactor

## Description

This pull request introduces a new "Must Visit Places" feature as Step 6 in the multi-step form. It includes the addition of a new component, backend integration for place suggestions, and UI updates to support the new step. Below are the most significant changes grouped by theme:

### New Feature: "Must Visit Places" Step

* Added a new component, `Step6Content`, which renders the `MustVisitPlacesContent` component. This component allows users to search for and add places they want to visit, with autocomplete suggestions and the ability to remove places. (`ui/src/components/forms/Step6Content.jsx`, [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-60e135b58ca24b1c9558d16fca4ae17b007ce951a9f8e03c794c1107def98861R1-R12); `ui/src/components/forms/step6/MustVisitPlacesContent.jsx`, [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-b7874d35f78a4d5c2454161059e7d4d6b56952b9dc1c50bcb6978769f1c0289dR1-R233)

### Integration with Multi-Step Form

* Updated `StepContent` to include Step 6 by importing `Step6Content` and adding it to the step-switching logic. (`ui/src/components/forms/StepContent.jsx`, [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-ec68d773bedaae2d692674a09db520bb5e1a0a3816849fd3009f64b3abc659caR7) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-ec68d773bedaae2d692674a09db520bb5e1a0a3816849fd3009f64b3abc659caR40-R41)
* Modified the `Forms` component to increase `totalSteps` to 6 and handle navigation to and from Step 6. (`ui/src/routes/Forms.jsx`, [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-6d2ae9226719b8b6af4af3fd67cfb11139fc2a9bf688e47bb9be3e49e69e6c1cL17-R17) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-6d2ae9226719b8b6af4af3fd67cfb11139fc2a9bf688e47bb9be3e49e69e6c1cL91-R94) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-6d2ae9226719b8b6af4af3fd67cfb11139fc2a9bf688e47bb9be3e49e69e6c1cR113-R116) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-6d2ae9226719b8b6af4af3fd67cfb11139fc2a9bf688e47bb9be3e49e69e6c1cR312-R318)

### Backend Integration and Data Handling

* Integrated `axiosPlace` for backend API calls to fetch autocomplete suggestions and place details for the "Must Visit Places" feature. (`ui/src/components/forms/step6/MustVisitPlacesContent.jsx`, [ui/src/components/forms/step6/MustVisitPlacesContent.jsxR1-R233](diffhunk://#diff-b7874d35f78a4d5c2454161059e7d4d6b56952b9dc1c50bcb6978769f1c0289dR1-R233))
* Added placeholder code to format and handle "Must Visit Places" data for potential backend submission. (`ui/src/routes/Forms.jsx`, [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-6d2ae9226719b8b6af4af3fd67cfb11139fc2a9bf688e47bb9be3e49e69e6c1cR140) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-6d2ae9226719b8b6af4af3fd67cfb11139fc2a9bf688e47bb9be3e49e69e6c1cR168-R174)

### UI Enhancements

* Implemented a responsive layout for the "Must Visit Places" step, including a search box with autocomplete, a list of suggestions, and a display of added places with images and delete functionality. (`ui/src/components/forms/step6/MustVisitPlacesContent.jsx`, [ui/src/components/forms/step6/MustVisitPlacesContent.jsxR1-R233](diffhunk://#diff-b7874d35f78a4d5c2454161059e7d4d6b56952b9dc1c50bcb6978769f1c0289dR1-R233))

These changes collectively enhance the multi-step form by introducing a new interactive step focused on planning travel destinations.

<!-- Reference any GitHub issues resolved by this PR -->

Related #3195 

## Introduced changes

<!-- A brief description of the changes -->

- The job `test-forge-unit-and-integration` is currently a bottleneck in the CI process, significantly delaying execution. This change partially fixes the problem by running integration tests with `cargo nextest`
- To avoid increasing the number of necessary workers, the number of partitions for E2E tests has been decreased from 8 to 3 as these jobs are still executed relatively quickly (around 10 minutes each)
- The entire workflow for both Windows and Ubuntu has improved from around [50 minutes](https://github.com/foundry-rs/starknet-foundry/actions/runs/14679406363) to [35 minutes](https://github.com/ddoktorski/starknet-foundry/actions/runs/14679518349)

body:
## Overview

This pull request implements the core smart contracts and documentation for the ZenPulse project, a blockchain-powered meditation app with personalized music, breathing exercises, and user rewards.

The key changes include:

- Creation of the `/workspace/README.md` file, which provides comprehensive documentation for the project, covering the overview, contract architecture, installation and setup instructions, usage guide, testing information, and security considerations.
- Modifications to the `/workspace/contracts/zenpulse-sessions.clar` contract to update the streak calculation to use block height instead of timestamp, replace timestamp-based operations with block-height for improved compatibility and deterministic behavior, and replace `stx-get-current-time-ms()` with block-height to estimate weekly intervals more reliably.
- Creation of the `/workspace/tests/zenpulse-sessions_test.ts` and `/workspace/tests/zenpulse-profile_test.ts` test suites to ensure comprehensive testing and validation of the core functionality.
- Creation of the `/workspace/contracts/zenpulse-sessions.clar` and `/workspace/contracts/zenpulse-profile.clar` smart contracts, which handle the core functionality of the ZenPulse application, including meditation session tracking and user profile management.

## Detailed Description

### /workspace/README.md
This new file provides comprehensive documentation for the ZenPulse project, covering the following sections:

- Project Overview: Describes the purpose and key features of the ZenPulse application.
- Contract Architecture: Explains the structure and responsibilities of the core smart contracts.
- Installation and Setup: Outlines the steps to set up the project and deploy the contracts.
- Usage Guide: Describes how users can interact with the ZenPulse application and its key functionality.
- Testing: Provides instructions for running the comprehensive test suites.
- Security Considerations: Highlights important security aspects and best practices.

### /workspace/contracts/zenpulse-sessions.clar
The changes made to this file include:

- Updating the streak calculation to use block height instead of timestamp, improving reliability and consistency.
- Replacing timestamp-based operations with block-height to ensure compatibility and deterministic behavior.
- Replacing `stx-get-current-time-ms()` with block-height to estimate weekly intervals more accurately.

These modifications will enhance the accuracy and robustness of the session tracking and reward distribution functionality.

### /workspace/tests/zenpulse-sessions_test.ts and /workspace/tests/zenpulse-profile_test.ts
These new test suites provide comprehensive coverage for the ZenPulse Sessions and Profile contracts, respectively. The tests cover the following aspects:

- Session logging and retrieval
- Streak tracking and reward distribution
- User profile creation, validation, updates, and mood history tracking

The addition of these test suites will improve the overall quality and maintainability of the codebase.

### /workspace/contracts/zenpulse-sessions.clar and /workspace/contracts/zenpulse-profile.clar
These new smart contracts implement the core functionality of the ZenPulse application, including:

- Meditation session tracking and reward management
- User profile creation, validation, and mood history tracking

The implementation of these contracts lays the foundation for the full ZenPulse application experience.

## Impact Analysis

The changes introduced in this pull request do not have any significant impact on the existing functionality of the ZenPulse application. The modifications are primarily focused on improving the reliability, testability, and documentation of the core components.

There are no known backward compatibility concerns, as the changes are additive in nature, introducing new functionality without modifying the existing behavior.

## Testing & Validation

The comprehensive test suites added in this pull request cover the key functionality of the ZenPulse Sessions and Profile contracts, ensuring the reliability and correctness of the core application logic.

To test the changes, you can run the following commands:

```
cd /workspace
clarinet test
```

The expected outcomes are:

- All tests in the `zenpulse-sessions_test.ts` and `zenpulse-profile_test.ts` suites should pass, indicating the proper functioning of the core contracts.
- The README.md file should be generated correctly, providing clear and detailed documentation for the project.

There are no known issues with the changes introduced in this pull request.

author: teal-bauer
body:
- Add SettingsService to manage persistent settings
- Store settings in both Redis and local config file
- Implement fallback mechanism for when Redis is unavailable
- Make config file path configurable via SCOOTUI_SETTINGS_PATH env var
- Update ThemeCubit and ScreenCubit to persist mode changes
- Update entry points to initialize environment configuration

On startup, configuration will be loaded from the config file (`settings.json`) and Redis, with Redis taking precedence:

```
flutter: 🔧 SettingsService: Loaded from file - {theme: dark, mode: navigation}
flutter: 🔧 SettingsService: Loading theme from Redis
flutter: 🔧 SettingsService: Redis theme = dark
flutter: 🔧 SettingsService: Loading mode from Redis
flutter: 🔧 SettingsService: Redis mode = navigation
flutter: 🔧 SettingsService: Loaded from Redis - {theme: dark, mode: navigation}
flutter: 🔧 SettingsService: Sync check - Redis theme = dark, settings = dark
flutter: 🔧 SettingsService: Sync check - Redis mode = navigation, settings = navigation
flutter: 🔧 SettingsService: Getting theme setting: dark
flutter: 🔧 SettingsService: Getting screen setting: navigation
flutter: 🔧 SettingsService: Final settings - Theme: ThemeMode.dark, Mode: navigation
```

Redis changes will also be reflected in the UI state:

```
redis> HSET dashboard mode navigation
redis> PUBLISH dashboard mode  #=> Dashboard goes to Map mode
```

   TensorFlow

    * C API:

Function `TfLiteOperatorCreate` was added recently, in TensorFlow Lite version 2.17.0, released on 7/11/2024, and we do not expect there will be much code using this function yet. Any code breakages can be easily resolved by passing nullptr as the new, 4th parameter.

* TensorRT support is disabled in CUDA builds for code health improvement.

* TensorFlow now supports and is compiled with NumPy 2.0 by default. Please see the [NumPy 2 release notes](https://numpy.org/doc/stable/release/2.0.0-notes.html) and the [NumPy 2 migration guide](https://numpy.org/devdocs/numpy_2_0_migration_guide.html#numpy-2-migration-guide).
  * Note that NumPy's type promotion rules have been changed(See [NEP 50](https://numpy.org/neps/nep-0050-scalar-promotion.html#nep50)for details). This may change the precision at which computations happen, leading either to type errors or to numerical changes to results.
  * Tensorflow will continue to support NumPy 1.26 until 2025, aligning with community standard deprecation timeline [here](https://scientific-python.org/specs/spec-0000/).

* Hermetic CUDA support is added.

  Hermetic CUDA uses a specific downloadable version of CUDA instead of the user’s locally installed CUDA. Bazel will download CUDA, CUDNN and NCCL distributions, and then use CUDA libraries and tools as dependencies in various Bazel targets. This enables more reproducible builds for Google ML projects and supported CUDA versions.

* Remove the `EnumNamesXNNPackFlags` function in `tensorflow/lite/acceleration/configuration/configuration_generated.h`.

  This change is a bug fix in the automatically generated code. This change is automatically generated by the new flatbuffer generator. The flatbuffers library is updated to 24.3.25 in https://github.com/tensorflow/tensorflow/commit/c17d64df85a83c1bd0fd7dcc0b1230812b0d3d48. The new flatbuffers library includes the following change https://github.com/google/flatbuffers/pull/7813 which fixed a underlying flatbuffer code generator bug.


 Known Caveats

 Major Features and Improvements

* `tf.data`
    * Add optional `synchronous` argument to `map`, to specify that the `map` should run synchronously, as opposed to be parallelizable when `options.experimental_optimization.map_parallelization=True`. This saves memory compared to setting `num_parallel_calls=1`.
    * Add optional `use_unbounded_threadpool` argument to `map`, to specify that the `map` should use an unbounded threadpool instead of the default pool that is based on the number of cores on the machine. This can improve throughput for map functions which perform IO or otherwise release the CPU.
    * Add [`tf.data.experimental.get_model_proto`](https://www.tensorflow.org/api_docs/python/tf/data/experimental/get_model_proto) to allow users to peek into the analytical model inside of a dataset iterator.

author: sinzii
body:
In big/complicated dapps (Polkadot Staking Dashboard or Polkadot Live), the number of operations sending to JSON-RPC server might be a lot at a time, this accidentally putting too much stress on the JSON-RPC server, especially smoldot/light-client causing it to hangup and not respond at all.

This PR introduce a `ThrottleQueue` to help ease up this issue, this will make sure there will be a certain number of concureny requests/operations can be send at a time and new requests/operations will be put in the queue waiting to be executed in line.

author: jozys
body:
This pull request introduces significant restructuring and new features to the project, focusing on modularizing the codebase, enhancing the Nearby Connections API integration, and refining the domain model. Key changes include the creation of new wrapper classes for Nearby Connections, the introduction of `Device` abstractions (`Master` and `Client`), and the reorganization of packages to better align with domain-driven design principles.

### Modularization and Domain Model Refinement:
* Reintroduced and relocated `ApplicationStatus` enum to the `domain` package with updated status values (`INIT`, `IDLE`, `DESTINATION`, `ACTIVE`, `ERROR`, `FINISHED`) for better alignment with the domain model (`app/src/main/java/de/schuettslaar/sensoration/domain/ApplicationStatus.kt`).
* Abstracted device behavior into a new `Device` class, with `Master` and `Client` subclasses implementing specific roles for advertising and discovering endpoints, respectively (`app/src/main/java/de/schuettslaar/sensoration/domain/Device.kt`, `Master.kt`, `Client.kt`). [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-a15bceb4d159de4e606b6b47681cdefddf77c21db03704849240ade7585d2b96R1-R40) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-81b140b2350723bca04294572b5c566bfa4d48efe4ae6d4a54959d2eb027a7acR1-R34) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-84f5361cce759cdf4f72860e2903174472d1e4a5f4b7dff6b11580a1fde1f74cR1-R40)

### Nearby Connections API Integration:
* Added `AdvertiseNearbyWrapper` and `DiscoverNearbyWrapper` classes to handle advertising and discovery functionalities using Google's Nearby Connections API (`app/src/main/java/de/schuettslaar/sensoration/adapter/nearby/AdvertiseNearbyWrapper.kt`, `DiscoverNearbyWrapper.kt`). [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-4b5902c61ddd9497954a611690b472e687227a7629bfc9cfb111d01ddc1c4febR1-R65) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-1bc188280f8feb8afa779fb03afe536fbf2b8811e028c703eea2c3b0acd00975R1-R84)
* Introduced a shared `NearbyWrapper` abstract class to encapsulate common logic for Nearby Connections, such as managing connection lifecycle callbacks and payload handling (`app/src/main/java/de/schuettslaar/sensoration/adapter/nearby/NearbyWrapper.kt`).

### Package Reorganization:
* Moved `ApplicationStatus`, `WrappedSensorData`, and sensor-related classes into the `domain` package to better reflect their roles in the domain layer (`app/src/main/java/de/schuettslaar/sensoration/domain`). [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-d12cb9c76a75aaef5bfff7021c4a8b953c8aab8aa30a14615edf84a995070f2aL1-R3) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-4ca0456a99e0c46d3655d8db6c86cd816b74852791b5481e80acb0197197630dR1-R10) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-aaea5158fab2c44a536a0288ce840ef7ef1cc7084bd40031fc67ac4a519fca33L1-R1)
* Renamed and relocated `NearbyStatus` to the `adapter/nearby` package to align with its role as part of the Nearby Connections integration (`app/src/main/java/de/schuettslaar/sensoration/adapter/nearby/NearbyStatus.kt`).

### Code Cleanup and Simplification:
* Removed the unused `ApplicationStatus` enum from its original location (`app/src/main/java/de/schuettslaar/sensoration/ApplicationStatus.kt`).
* Deleted the obsolete `NavigationHost` implementation, likely replaced by a more modular navigation solution (`app/src/main/java/de/schuettslaar/sensoration/navigation/NavigationHost.kt`).

These changes collectively improve the maintainability, scalability, and clarity of the codebase while introducing new capabilities for handling device connections and data transfer.

body:
The old TFG finder did not properly walk through all possible paths in case of nested cycles and converging flows.
This problem is now solved and the TFG finder also allows for setting a custom cycle depth.

As a consequence, the number of TFGs created from e.g. sqshq_18 climbed from 90 to 17933. I performed manual checks on 10 of these TFGs and they were valid. Duplicates were also ruled out. 

This forced me to disable the evaluation of the MicroSecEndTest Models for now. While the creation of the TFGs takes under a second, copying and evaluating 17000 TFGs takes time.

The efficiency of the new algorithm also makes the DFDSimpleFinder obsolete and it can be removed in a further commit.

body:
This PR introduces several significant improvements to SvelteBench that enhance both performance and accuracy of the benchmark tests.

### Key Improvements

**Performance Enhancements**

 • Concurrency Support: Added a concurrency limit feature that allows multiple tests to run in parallel, significantly reducing overall benchmark execution time
 • Implemented via the runWithConcurrencyLimit utility in src/utils/parallel.ts

**Prompt Engineering Improvements**

 • Modular Prompt System: Restructured prompts to be loaded from markdown files:
    • System prompt now loaded from src/prompts/system-prompt.md
    • Context information loaded from src/prompts/context-prompt.md
    • Test-specific prompts remain in their respective directories
 • Proper System Instructions: Instructions are now submitted as system messages rather than being prepended to the user prompt, which better aligns with LLM best practices
 • Context Prompt Support: Added ability to include contextual documents that provide background information to the LLM without cluttering the main prompt

**Test Improvements**

 • Fixed 'inspect' Test: Resolved issues with the 'inspect' test that was too specific and consistently failing
 • Improved Instructions Quality: Enhanced the clarity and specificity of instructions to yield more accurate code generation

**Technical Implementation**

 • Added utility functions for loading prompts from files
 • Implemented a parallel execution system with configurable concurrency limits
 • Updated LLM provider implementations to properly use system prompts
 • Refactored test runner to support the new prompt structure

These changes should result in faster benchmark runs and more consistent, higher quality code generation from the tested LLMs.

author: chadlwilson
body:
There should be no need to ever encrypt with DES anymore; we only support decryption during migration to AES. Accordingly, we can replace the only other usage of BouncyCastle (to verify update packet RSA signing) with basic usage of default crypto libraries, since the public key is in a known format bundled with the server.

This also removes an ancient cipher updater which ran at start-up to remove an insecure old DES cipher and re-encrypt. This should not be required now, as the config migrater should remove all DES encryption and convert to AES anyway, regardless of whether the original DES cipher is safe or not.

Contemplated removing the DES migration support entirely, as it's ancient, but decided not to in the end, since it's not too big a deal to keep right now, given BouncyCastle isn't necessary.

author: globalkmaria
body:
## What this PR does

This PR fixes a hydration error that occurs in the `examples/nextjs-app-prefetching` example, specifically in the React Example: Nextjs App Prefetching documentation.

**Changes made:**
- Added `await` before `queryClient.prefetchQuery` on the server to ensure data fetching completes before `dehydrate(queryClient)`.

## Why

While visiting the [TanStack Query documentation example](https://tanstack.com/query/latest/docs/framework/react/examples/nextjs-app-prefetching),  
I encountered the following error:

```
⨯ Error: Missing queryFn: ‘[“pokemon”]’
at Array.forEach ()
{ digest: ‘1532731130’ }
```

This happened because:

- `prefetchQuery` was not awaited on the server, so `dehydrate(queryClient)` serialized a query still in "pending" state.
- In TanStack Query, during dehydration, **only `queryKey` and `state` are serialized**.  
  **The `queryFn` is never serialized**, because JavaScript functions cannot be transferred via JSON.  
- Therefore, when the client hydrated and used `useSuspenseQuery`, the QueryClient had the `queryKey` but no associated `queryFn`, causing a `Missing queryFn` error.

This PR ensures that:
- Prefetching is completed before dehydration.
- The same `QueryClient` instance is used consistently across server and client.
- Hydration succeeds without missing functions.
- Suspense works properly with server-prefetched queries.

## Testing

- Ran `examples/nextjs-app-router` locally.
- Verified:
  - No hydration errors occur after the fix.
  - Immediate rendering with prehydrated data.
  - Correct fallback loading UI when no prefetch exists.
- No runtime errors or warnings observed.

## Notes

- This fix is isolated to the example app; no core TanStack Query code is changed.
- Improves the developer onboarding experience by preventing a common hydration pitfall when using `useSuspenseQuery` and Next.js App Router together.
- Based on the current React Query v5 behavior where only `queryKey` and `state` are serialized during dehydration.

---

Thank you for maintaining such a great project! 🚀
Happy to adjust anything based on reviewer feedback.

Once upon a time, a backend developer and a machine learning engineer were working on the same project: an app that recommended the perfect pizza topping based on your mood.

The backend dev proudly said, "I've built a perfectly efficient, lightning-fast API. Every request returns in under 100 milliseconds."
The ML engineer grinned and said, "Amazing! I just finished training a neural network that predicts toppings with 99.9% accuracy!"

Feeling excited, they deployed everything. First user logs in, says they're feeling "melancholic," and the app immediately recommends pineapple and anchovies.

Backend dev: "Hey, at least the API was fast."
ML engineer: "And it was accurate! The model loves pineapple and anchovies for sadness!"
User: uninstalls app immediately

author: h4vox
body:
# Tests for BigInteger Parsing Across Cultures (powershell#25396)

## Overview
This PR adds **unit tests** for verifying `BigInteger` parsing across different **cultures and number formats**. The tests ensure PowerShell correctly converts numbers with various thousands separators, including:
- **Comma (`1,000`)** → Used in `en-US`, `hi-IN`
- **Space (`1 000`)** → Used in `ru-RU`, `fr-FR`, `sv-SE`
- **Indian number format (`1,00,000`)** → Used in `hi-IN`

The tests dynamically fetch the correct **`NumberGroupSeparator`** based on the **current locale** to prevent parsing errors seen in older PowerShell versions.

## Changes Included
- **Added test file:** `test/powershell/engine/BigIntegerCultureHandling.Tests.ps1`
- **Uses Pester for structured validation**
- **Verifies PowerShell correctly handles thousands-separated numbers**
- **Ensures compatibility across multiple cultures (`en-US`, `hi-IN`, `fr-FR`, etc.)**

## Related PRs
This PR adds necessary tests for **PR #25396**, ensuring full validation of numeric parsing behavior.

author: okehtimothy44
body:
## Overview
This pull request introduces the initial implementation of the Time Snap NFT contract, a comprehensive SIP-009 compliant time-limited NFT contract with robust security and time-based validation features. The key changes include:

- SIP-009 compliant NFT contract with time-based expiration and renewal mechanisms
- Minting, validity checking, renewal, and transfer functions
- Comprehensive test suite covering all major functionalities

The contract provides a secure and flexible way to create time-limited digital collectibles on the Stacks blockchain.

## Detailed Description
### README.md
This file provides an overview of the Time Snap NFT project, including the project's purpose, key features, contract architecture, installation and setup instructions, usage guide, testing information, and security considerations. It covers all the key aspects that a developer would need to understand in order to use and contribute to this project.

### `/contracts/time_snap_nft.clar`
This file contains the implementation of the time-limited NFT contract. The key changes include:
- Reverting to local trait import and removing the external trait definition
- Adding explicit trait import to resolve the undeclared trait error
- Adding a definition for the time-snap-nft non-fungible token to allow minting and transferring
- Updating trait import to use local import syntax
- Creating a comprehensive SIP-009 compliant time-limited NFT contract with robust security and time-based validation features

### `/tests/time_snap_nft_test.ts`
This file contains a comprehensive test suite for the TimeSnap NFT contract, validating all major functionalities such as minting, time validity, renewal, transfer, and security checks.

## Impact Analysis
The introduction of the time-limited NFT contract and test suite does not impact any existing functionality, as this is a new feature being added to the project. The contract is designed to be compatible with the SIP-009 standard, ensuring that it can be easily integrated with other Stacks blockchain-based applications.

## Testing & Validation
The comprehensive test suite in the `/tests/time_snap_nft_test.ts` file covers all major functionalities of the time-limited NFT contract, including:
- Minting a new NFT
- Checking the time validity of the NFT
- Renewing the NFT
- Transferring the NFT
- Security checks

To test the changes, you can run the test suite using the following command:
```
npm run test
```

The expected outcome is that all tests should pass, validating the correct implementation of the time-limited NFT contract.
